turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_target_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_target_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have a yield strength CLOSEST to 1051 MPa — not the highest, the closest to that value — then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training targets reach a maximum of only ~908 MPa, so 1051 MPa lies in the extrapolation regime. Consequently the five pool members whose feature vectors lie closest to the highest-strength training examples are expected to receive the highest model predictions and therefore the smallest |ŷ − 1051|.

Direct nearest-neighbour matches (identical heat-treatment/route, composition and process variables within a few tenths of a percent / a few tens of °C) are:

- c079 ≃ 908 MPa example (QT + AM, high V/Co/Cu),
- c017 ≃ 864 MPa example (QT + wrought),
- c008 ≃ 738 MPa example (QT + cast, high-Cr low-Ni),
- c033 ≃ same 738 MPa neighbourhood (slightly higher Ni/Cr),
- c039 ≃ 722 MPa example (QT + wrought, high-Ni low-Cr).

All other pool rows are substantially farther from any training point above 700 MPa and are therefore predicted lower. Ranking by these analogue strengths yields the five candidates closest to the 1051 MPa target.

Final: c079, c017, c008, c033, c039
